## Goal

Complete #2848 and #2868 against current PyPTO main and PTOAS v0.67, preserving their separate frontend goals. Related: #2754, #2832, and hw-native-sys/PTOAS#1575.

## Contract and scope

- #2848 converts static logical FP4 shapes and coordinates to FP4E2M1X2 byte-carrier units after SSA flattening. Preserve logical tensor.dim results without violating NoNestedCalls.
- #2868 permits zero-copy, same-shape FP4E2M1X2 aliases with UINT8/INT8 so models can reshape byte views. Keep logical FP4 aliases, other dtype pairs, and direct FP4-family reshape rejected.
- PyPTO GM views, partitions, offsets, and strides stay in carrier units. PTOAS v0.67 performs ISA nibble conversion only at transfer consumers; avoid duplicate expansion.
- Synchronize the pinned compiler version, runtime minimum, regression tests, and English/Chinese documentation. Keep the existing runtime/pto-isa pin unless validation demonstrates that a separate update is required.

## Acceptance

- Both original fork branches contain one cohesive commit on current main, with reviewable diffs and no merge conflicts.
- Build from each checkout; pass unit tests, relevant compiler/system regressions, lint, type checks, and PR CI.
- Cover multi-row transfers and nonzero packed-axis offsets, consumed byte-alias/reshape round trips, and supported memory planners.
- Evaluate existing review feedback, reply with verified results, and resolve remaining threads. Report device access or upstream limitations explicitly.

Native FP4 matrix operations, dynamic logical FP4 packing, distributed FP4, and pypto-lib model changes remain outside these PRs.

### Component

Codegen

### Description

On Ascend 910B with `memory_planner=MemoryPlanner.PTOAS`, a narrowing `tile.cast` that needs scratch reaches ptoas in its **implicit-tmp** form with dynamic tile shapes, and ptoas cannot size the scratch:

```text
'pto.tcvt' op requires static tile_buf shapes to materialize implicit tcvt tmp
```

The cause is that two gates disagree about which axis they are on.

`InitMemRef` materializes the level-3 explicit scratch only for the PyPTO and DSA-RP planners — `src/ir/transforms/init_memref.cpp:1054`:

```cpp
const MemoryPlanner planner = ctx ? ctx->GetMemoryPlanner() : MemoryPlanner::PyPTO;
if (handler != nullptr && (planner == MemoryPlanner::PyPTO || planner == MemoryPlanner::DsaRP)) {
    MaterializePtoLevel3ScratchMutator materializer(handler->RequiresLevel3TmpScratch());
```

Codegen, however, branches on the **per-architecture** `RequiresLevel3TmpScratch()` — `src/backend/common/pto_ops_elementwise.cpp:458`:

```cpp
if (op->args_.size() == 2 && codegen.GetBackendHandler()->RequiresLevel3TmpScratch()) {
    ...
    RequireStaticValidShapeForPtoas(src_type, "tile.cast", "src", op->span_);
    const std::string src_ssa = EnsureStaticViewTileSsa(op->args_[0], codegen, "tcvt_src_view");
```

`RequiresLevel3TmpScratch()` is `true` on a2a3 and `false` on a5 (`include/pypto/backend/910B/backend_910b_handler.h:51`, `include/pypto/backend/950/backend_950_handler.h:55`), whose documented rationale is "False on Ascend950: PTOAS level-2 PlanMemory owns implicit tmp instead."

The two gates were implicitly correlated: level-3 explicit scratch (a2a3) went together with the PyPTO/DSA-RP planners, and implicit tmp (a5) with level 2. **`a2a3 × PTOAS` breaks the correlation.** `InitMemRef` appends no tmp operand, so `op->args_.size()` stays 1, the codegen branch is not taken, and neither the tmp nor the static views (`EnsureStaticViewTileSsa`) are emitted — which is exactly what ptoas needs in order to materialize the implicit tmp itself.

### Steps to Reproduce

Compile-time failure, so no NPU is needed.

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$(pwd)/python:$PYTHONPATH

python -m pytest tests/st/runtime/ops/test_cast_saturation.py \
  --platform=a2a3 --memory-planner=ptoas --precompile-workers=4 \
  --save-kernels --kernels-dir /tmp/ptoas
```

Affected case:

- `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_cast_saturation.py::TestCastSaturation::test_in_range_values_agree_across_modes[off]`

Only `saturation_mode=off` fails; the other seven cases in the file pass, because only the non-saturating FP16 to INT8 helper takes scratch.

### Expected Behavior

The kernel compiles. Either `InitMemRef` materializes the explicit scratch on a2a3 regardless of planner (the architecture still requires level-3 scratch), or codegen bridges the implicit form to static views so ptoas can size the tmp itself.

### Actual Behavior

```text
ptoas compilation failed: loc("tests/st/runtime/ops/test_cast_saturation.py":80:9):
error: 'pto.tcvt' op requires static tile_buf shapes to materialize implicit tcvt tmp
Error: Pass execution failed.
```

Emitted `.pto` under PTOAS — one operand, dynamic shapes, no scratch:

```text
%quantized__ssa_v0 = pto.alloc_tile valid_row = %c1_index valid_col = %c128_index : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=1, cols=128, v_row=?, v_col=?, ...>
pto.tcvt ins(%tile__ssa_v0 {rmode = #pto<round_mode TRUNC>, satmode = #pto<saturation_mode OFF>} : !pto.tile_buf<..., v_row=?, v_col=?, ...>) outs(%quantized__ssa_v0 : ...)
```

Emitted `.pto` under PyPTO — scratch allocated, static views bridged, two-operand form:

```text
%quantized__tcvt_tmp_v0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c256_i64 valid_row = %c1_index valid_col = %c256_index : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=1, cols=256, ...>
%tcvt_src_view = pto.treshape %tile__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<..., v_row=?, v_col=?, ...> -> !pto.tile_buf<..., v_row=1, v_col=128, ...>
%tcvt_tmp_view = pto.treshape %quantized__tcvt_tmp_v0 : ... -> !pto.tile_buf<..., v_row=1, v_col=256, ...>
%tcvt_dst_view = pto.treshape %quantized__ssa_v0 : ... -> !pto.tile_buf<..., v_row=1, v_col=128, ...>
pto.tcvt ins(%tcvt_src_view, %tcvt_tmp_view {...}) outs(%tcvt_dst_view : ...)
```

### Git Commit ID

33476eadb4bd5cb3b505b748d402a6346d1b1a35

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #2557 is the **mirror image** of this bug on the other axis. Its title — "level3 tmp bridge is gated on arch, not build level" — describes `tsort32` failing on a5 because the static-view rebinding branch is gated off by architecture. This report is the planner axis of the same gating problem, on a2a3. Whoever fixed #2557 is likely the right reviewer.

Found while validating a suite-wide switch of the system tests to the ptoas planner: #2847.
title: [Bug] InitMemRef skips tcvt scratch materialization on a2a3 under memory_planner=PTOAS

### Component

Codegen

### Description

#2873 keeps the **all-zero** valid_shape sentinel dynamic in a view type string, so it no
longer renders `v_row=0, v_col=0`. A valid_shape with a **single** zero beside a real
extent is not covered and still renders a static zero.

pto-isa declares the two accessors per dimension — `GetValidRow` keys on `RowMask` alone,
`GetValidCol` on `ColMask` alone:

```cpp
// pto-isa @ runtime/pto_isa.pin = 3b4faf67a, include/pto/common/pto_tile.hpp
template <int ColMask = ValidCol>
AICORE static constexpr std::enable_if_t<(ColMask > 0), unsigned> GetValidCol()
template <int ColMask = ValidCol>
AICORE std::enable_if_t<ColMask == DYNAMIC, unsigned> GetValidCol() const
```

So `Tile<..., 8, 0, ...>` matches no `GetValidCol` overload, exactly as
`Tile<..., 0, 0, ...>` matched no `GetValidRow` overload in #2870.

`IsZeroValidShapeSentinel` matches only the all-zero form, and its doc comment states that
a partially narrowed extent "is a genuine shape and is left alone". That is true of its
*semantics* but not of its *representability*: a static zero in either dimension has no
static encoding in pto-isa.

**No pass is known to produce a single-zero valid_shape** — `WithZeroValidShape` stamps
every dimension, so it only ever produces the all-zero form. The trigger demonstrated
below is user-authored DSL. This is therefore a latent gap, filed so the scope limit in
#2873 is recorded rather than re-derived.

### Steps to Reproduce

**1. DSL -> `.pto`** (`memory_planner=PTOAS`, verified at `63f1b66c` i.e. with #2873 applied):

```python
src: pl.Tile[[16, 8], pl.FP32, pl.MemorySpace.Vec, pl.TileView(valid_shape=[8, 0])] = (
    pl.tile.create([16, 8], dtype=pl.FP32, target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
)
view: pl.Tile[[16, 8], pl.INT32] = pl.tile.reinterpret_view(src, pl.INT32)
back: pl.Tile[[16, 8], pl.FP32] = pl.cast(view, pl.FP32)
return pl.store(back, [0, 0], out)
```

```text
%reinterpret_view_buf = pto.treshape %src__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<..., dtype=f32, v_row=?, v_col=?>
                                                 -> !pto.tile_buf<..., dtype=i32, v_row=8, v_col=0>
pto.tcvt ins(%reinterpret_view_buf ... : !pto.tile_buf<..., dtype=i32, v_row=8, v_col=0>) outs(...)
```

Rendering by valid_shape, same program shape:

| `valid_shape` | treshape result type |
| --- | --- |
| `[0, 0]` | `v_row=?, v_col=?` — #2873 working |
| `[0, 8]` | **`v_row=0`**, `v_col=8` |
| `[8, 0]` | `v_row=8`, **`v_col=0`** |
| `[8, 8]` | `v_row=8, v_col=8` |

**2. `.pto` -> generated C++** (`ptoas 0.65 --enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level2`). The
DSL program above also produces a zero-extent `pto.partition_view` for its store, which
ptoas rejects first, so this step uses a minimal module whose consumer is `pto.trecip`:

```text
%a = pto.alloc_tile valid_row = %c16_index valid_col = %c8_index : <f32, rows=16, cols=8, v_row=?, v_col=?>
%v = pto.treshape %a : <... v_row=?, v_col=?> -> <... v_row=8, v_col=0>
%b = pto.alloc_tile valid_row = %c16_index valid_col = %c8_index : <f32, rows=16, cols=8, v_row=?, v_col=?>
pto.trecip ins(%v : <... v_row=8, v_col=0>) outs(%b : <... v_row=?, v_col=?>)
```

```cpp
// v_row=8, v_col=8  ->
Tile<TileType::Vec, float, 16, 8, BLayout::RowMajor,  8,  8, ...> v8;
// v_row=8, v_col=0  ->
Tile<TileType::Vec, float, 16, 8, BLayout::RowMajor,  8,  0, ...> v8;   // ColMask = 0
// v_row=?, v_col=?  ->
Tile<TileType::Vec, float, 16, 8, BLayout::RowMajor, -1, -1, ...> v8;
```

**3. Overload resolution.** ccec was not run (no device compiler on the reporting host), so
the final step is reproduced with host `g++ -std=c++17 -fsyntax-only` against the two
declarations copied verbatim from the pinned header:

```text
error: no matching function for call to 'Tile<8, 0>::GetValidCol()'
note: candidate: template<int ColMask> static constexpr enable_if_t<(ColMask > 0), unsigned> GetValidCol()
note:   template argument deduction/substitution failed:
        ... enable_if_t<_Cond = false> ... [with int ColMask = 0]
```

`Tile<8, 8>` and `Tile<8, -1>` both resolve; only `Tile<8, 0>` fails.

### Expected Behavior

PyPTO does not hand a statically-zero valid extent to a static view annotation in **any**
dimension. Either such a valid_shape is rejected where it is produced, or the affected
dimension keeps the dynamic annotation.

### Actual Behavior

The affected dimension renders a static zero, which becomes an unsatisfiable `RowMask` /
`ColMask` template argument in the generated in-core C++.

### Git Commit ID

63f1b66c676ab56cc2abee62bfd513189168cfec

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

**Making the dimension dynamic is not obviously the right fix**, which is why #2873 scoped
itself to the all-zero form rather than relaxing per dimension.

`pto.treshape` takes no `valid_row` / `valid_col` operands, so ptoas default-constructs its
destination tile from the result type. That default constructor is pto-isa's
"constructor for static shape" and never assigns `RowMaskInternal` / `ColMaskInternal`,
which are bare `unsigned` members with no default initializer. A dynamic annotation
therefore lowers to a read of an **uninitialized** valid extent, not a guaranteed zero.

For the all-zero sentinel that is safe because the replay lane discards the result. For a
single zero of unknown origin it is not: it would trade today's compile error for a silent
read of an uninitialized extent.

So the useful next step is to establish where a single-zero valid_shape can come from:

- if only user-authored DSL can produce one, reject it at the authoring boundary;
- if a pass can produce one, that pass is likely the actual defect;
- only if it turns out to be another "compute nothing" marker does the per-dimension
  dynamic annotation become correct.

Related: #2870 (the all-zero form), #2873 (its fix), #2557 (the same static-view / valid-extent
annotation machinery, gated on a different axis).
title: [Bug] A single zero valid dimension still reaches the static PTOAS view annotation

### Component

Codegen

### Description

Under `memory_planner=MemoryPlanner.PTOAS`, `tile.fillpad_inplace` emits a `pto.tfillpad` whose `ins` and `outs` are the **same** SSA value, typed `pad=0`. ptoas rejects it with `expects dst PadVal != Null for tfillpad`.

The in-place semantics are expressed as a *shared UB address* — `src/backend/common/pto_ops_elementwise.cpp:1020` says so directly:

```cpp
// Inplace variant: set_output_reuses_input(0) makes src/dst share UB addr.
{"tile.fillpad_inplace", "pto.tfillpad",         1},
```

Under the PyPTO planner, `AllocateMemoryAddr` gives the source (`pad=0`) and the padded destination (`pad=1`) the same address while keeping them two distinct SSA values with distinct types. On the PTOAS path there are no addresses, so the aliasing collapses onto one SSA value — and with it the destination's `pad=1` type is lost.

The `pad` value lives in the `tile_buf` **type**, not in the address, so one SSA value cannot carry both.

### Steps to Reproduce

Compile-time failure, so no NPU is needed.

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$(pwd)/python:$PYTHONPATH

# Fails
python -m pytest tests/st/runtime/ops/test_fillpad_inplace.py \
  --platform=a2a3 --memory-planner=ptoas --precompile-workers=4 \
  --save-kernels --kernels-dir /tmp/ptoas

# Passes, for comparison
python -m pytest tests/st/runtime/ops/test_fillpad_inplace.py \
  --platform=a2a3 --memory-planner=pypto --precompile-workers=4 \
  --save-kernels --kernels-dir /tmp/pypto

diff /tmp/ptoas/fillpad_inplace_zero@a2a3@ptoas/ptoas/*.pto \
     /tmp/pypto/fillpad_inplace_zero@a2a3@pypto/ptoas/*.pto
```

Affected cases (all three fail):

- `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_fillpad_inplace.py::TestFillpadInplace::test_fillpad_inplace_max[a2a3]`
- `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_fillpad_inplace.py::TestFillpadInplace::test_fillpad_inplace_min[a2a3]`
- `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_fillpad_inplace.py::TestFillpadInplace::test_fillpad_inplace_zero[a2a3]`

### Expected Behavior

The kernel compiles, and ptoas emits the in-place form of the instruction, as it does under the PyPTO planner.

### Actual Behavior

```text
ptoas compilation failed: loc("tests/st/runtime/ops/test_fillpad_inplace.py":44:51):
error: expects dst PadVal != Null for tfillpad
Error: Failed to parse MLIR.
```

Emitted `.pto` under PTOAS — one value, `pad=0` on both sides:

```text
%tile__ssa_v0 = pto.alloc_tile valid_row = %c48_index valid_col = %c64_index : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=64, cols=64, ..., pad=0>
pto.tfillpad ins(%tile__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<..., pad=0>) outs(%tile__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<..., pad=0>)
```

Emitted `.pto` under PyPTO — two values at the same address, `pad=0` and `pad=1`:

```text
%tile__ssa_v0        = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c0_i64 valid_row = %c48_index valid_col = %c64_index : !pto.tile_buf<..., pad=0>
%padded_tile__ssa_v0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c0_i64 valid_row = %c64_index valid_col = %c64_index : !pto.tile_buf<..., pad=1>
pto.tfillpad ins(%tile__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<..., pad=0>) outs(%padded_tile__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf<..., pad=1>)
```

### Git Commit ID

33476eadb4bd5cb3b505b748d402a6346d1b1a35

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

**The dialect can express this; the fix looks small and is on the PyPTO side.** I hand-edited the failing `.pto` and re-ran the pinned ptoas 0.64 at `--pto-level=level2`:

| Variant | ptoas result |
| ------- | ------------ |
| As emitted (`ins`/`outs` the same `pad=0` value) | `expects dst PadVal != Null for tfillpad` |
| `outs` type annotation relabelled to `pad=1` | `use of value expects different type than prior uses` — one SSA value cannot hold two types |
| **`pto.treshape` from `pad=0` to `pad=1`, fill into that view** | **compiles** |
| A second `alloc_tile` with `pad=1` as destination | compiles, but as two buffers |

The generated C++ shows the `treshape` spelling is the semantically correct one — ptoas recognises the aliasing by itself:

```cpp
// treshape variant
TFILLPAD<pto::TFillPadMode::InPlace>(v29, v23);

// second-allocation variant
TFILLPAD(v30, v24);
```

PyPTO already owns this mechanism: `EnsureTileViewSsa` / `EnsureStaticViewTileSsa` bridge exactly this way for `tcvt`, `tprelu` and `tcolsum`. It is simply not applied to `tile.fillpad_inplace` on the PTOAS path.

Found while validating a suite-wide switch of the system tests to the ptoas planner: #2847.
title: [Bug] tile.fillpad_inplace loses the destination pad value under memory_planner=PTOAS

本文记录尚未完成同名系统测试（system test，ST）验收的 PTOAS op 实施路线及批次验收事实。当前接口与覆盖状态以 [PTOAS Op 状态矩阵](ptoas-op-status.md) 为唯一来源；“代码或 ST 文件已添加”不等于“已完成”。只有生成的 `.pto` 包含最新 PTOAS canonical op 名且至少一个支持平台上的真机 ST 通过后，状态矩阵中的 ST 才能改为 `✅`；尚未真机验证的其他架构必须继续在备注和 G3 中记录。

接口名称以最新 PTOAS `main` `d852dd2dba3e5bf7a69ce8324eb88afc336e8a33` 为准。本计划的原始范围为 67 个无同名真机 ST 的 op；B01 完成 A2/A3 真机验收后，状态矩阵当前剩余 62 个。B01 仍保留在批次表和验收记录中，但不再计入下方“无 ST op 分类”。不适合独立 ST 的内部或 legacy op 不在计划内。每个实现批次仍须先用 PyPTO 当前固定的 PTOAS `v0.48` 做最小组装验证；若接口只存在于更新版本，应先单独升级工具链，不把版本升级与 op 实现混在同一个 PR。

## 无 ST op 分类

分类沿用状态矩阵中的 op 类别；下表 62 项与状态矩阵中 `ST测试` 或 `distributed ST测试` 为 `❌` 的行严格一一对应。

## B01 实施与验收记录

B01 的源码、UT 和五份同名 ST 已落盘。当前矩阵的 A2/A3 真机任务在 device 5 上分三批执行：`task_20260727_012033_6845730792`（32/32）、`task_20260727_012037_7177622613`（32/32）和 `task_20260727_012039_7236615809`（1/1），合计 65/65 通过，因此状态矩阵的五项已改为 `✅`。A5 真机尚未执行，继续作为跨平台 G3 待办；ST 不使用 skip 或 xfail 隐藏接口差异。

| `pto.trowmin` | tile 与 tensor lowering；`i16/i32/f16/f32`；必选 `tmp` 的 exact/oversized 安全形式；full、三种 tail、valid `1×1` 最小非零边界及 oversized tmp + combined tail；首/中/尾及重复最小值，invalid tail 放置更小 poison | PyPTO 主动保持 DN 输出及 A2/A3 安全的 same-dtype、同 rank、足量 workspace 子集；legacy ND 输出和 A5 relaxed placeholder 暂不作为公共运行时承诺 | `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_row_min.py` |

| 门槛 | B01 当前结果 |

| G1 IR/API | 已补齐 precision、可选 `tmp`、packed carrier、按可执行接口收紧的 dtype/physical-shape/layout/valid-shape 约束、mixed scalar/cast lowering、旧位置参数兼容及负向 UT |
| G2 exact codegen | exact-op UT 通过；A2/A3 目标 65/65、A5 目标 81/81 个 codegen-only case 通过 PTOAS 组装 |
| G3 真机 ST | **A2/A3 已完成**：device 5 真机分三批执行，任务 `task_20260727_012033_6845730792`（32/32）、`task_20260727_012037_7177622613`（32/32）、`task_20260727_012039_7236615809`（1/1），合计 65/65 通过；PTOAS `v0.48`，runtime 固定 PTO-ISA `83d01313`。A5 真机尚未执行；`a2a3sim` 65/65、`a5sim` 76/76 通过，A5 `i8` 的 5 个 `trowexpandadd` case 因 CPU simulator stub 限制仅完成 device-target 组装 |

| 范围 | 来源 | 移植规则 |
|---|---|---|
| `tdiv/tsubs/tlog/trowmin/trowexpandadd/tsels` | `e6ae95b2` | 只移植这 6 项；`tadds`、`texpands`、`tmrgsort` 已在主线有 ST，不重复带回 |
| `tgatherb`, `ttri` | `feat-add-ptoas-ops-batch5`，核心提交 `64c6b160`, `ee7b686a` | 分成两个 PR，保留 byte-offset 与 diagonal 语义 |
| `mgather` | `issue-1807-loop-local-gather`，核心提交 `711e45c7`, `7ec0e5f2` | 把旧 `pto.tmgather` 映射修为 `pto.mgather`，去掉 skip 后按当前工具链复验 |
| GEMV 三项 | `fix-pr1823-op-isa-gaps` / `5c106339` | 适配当前 memory/layout 实现，覆盖 1-row Mat、窄 K、BF16/FP16 |
| `tprelu` 与 carry | `fix-pr1823-pypto-codegen-ops` 未提交 worktree | `tprelu` 保持 `(src, slope, tmp)` 三参数；验证 carry 的真实算式和 alias 规则 |

旧分支的 backend 代码基于单体 `pto_ops_common.cpp`，不得整分支 cherry-pick；应把相关 hunk 手工适配到当前 `pto_ops_elementwise.cpp`、`pto_ops_datamove.cpp`、`pto_ops_memory.cpp` 或 `pto_ops_distributed.cpp`。`pto.trandom` 已通过 `ff8028d0` 合入，不属于本计划。

## 受影响代码层检查表

| 层 | 典型文件 | 何时必改 |
|---|---|---|
| PTOAS 兼容性 | `toolchain/versions.env`；最小 `.pto` probe | 每个 op 都先验证；需要 bump 时另开 PR |
| C++ tile IR / type inference | `src/ir/op/tile_ops/*.cpp`, `src/ir/op/type_inference.cpp` | 新 op、签名/shape/dtype/memory-space 变化 |
| Tensor API / lowering | `src/ir/op/tensor_ops/*.cpp`, `src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp` | 只有具备稳定 tensor 语义的 op 才增加 |
| Distributed IR | `src/ir/op/distributed/*.cpp` | comm session/event、collective 或 system op |
| Python IR / DSL / exports | `python/pypto/ir/op/{tile,tensor}_ops.py`, `python/pypto/language/op/{tile,tensor,unified}_ops.py` 及相关 `__init__.py` | 公共 API 或签名变化 |
| PTO codegen | `src/backend/common/pto_ops_{elementwise,datamove,memory,distributed}.cpp`，必要时 `pto_ops_shared.cpp` | 精确 op 名、operand 顺序、属性、enum、in-place outs、tmp 规则 |
| Layout / memory passes | `src/ir/transforms/infer_tile_memory_space_pass.cpp`, `resolve_backend_op_layouts_pass.cpp` 等 | GEMV、MX、FP/scaling、alias/layout 特殊约束 |
| UT | `tests/ut/ir/operators/`, `tests/ut/ir/transforms/`, `tests/ut/language/`, `tests/ut/codegen/` | IR/DSL/type/conversion/codegen 均需对应断言 |
| 真机 ST | `tests/st/runtime/ops/`, `tests/st/distributed/` | 数值或可观察行为验证，并确认最终 `.pto` 含精确同名 op |
| 文档 | `docs/zh-cn/dev/ir/05-operators.md`、中文 distributed 文档、`docs/zh-cn/dev/ptoas-op-status.md` | PR 合入后同步中文 API 文档与状态证据 |

## ST 覆盖要求

每个新增 op 的 ST 必须覆盖最新 PTOAS 文档定义的**全部语义分支**，不能只选一个典型 case。提交时应逐项列出并覆盖该 op 适用的全部 overload/签名、dtype 族、可选 operand、属性或 mode、`tmp` 有无、in-place/alias 规则、memory space、layout 以及架构差异；PTOAS 明确不支持的组合须附 manual 或 verifier 依据，不能以 skip/xpass 代替覆盖。

凡 operand 或 result 使用 tile 且接口允许 `valid_shape`，ST 还必须包含 `valid_shape` case：

- 覆盖 `valid_shape == shape` 的完整 tile，以及 `valid_shape < shape` 的非完整 tile。
- 若行、列均可独立裁剪，分别覆盖 row tail、column tail 和 row+column tail。
- reference 只在 valid region 内比较数值；若 PTOAS 对 invalid region 有明确行为，也必须验证该行为。
- 若某 op 确实不适用或不支持 `valid_shape`，须在测试或 PR 中写明依据，不得直接遗漏。

上述 case matrix 全部通过后，该 op 才能在状态矩阵中标记为有 ST。

## 固定验收门槛

- [ ] **G0 接口与版本**：核对最新 PTOAS canonical name；用 PyPTO pinned PTOAS 组装最小 `.pto`；记录支持架构、dtype、shape、layout、memory space 与 scratch 条件。
- [ ] **G1 IR/API**：C++ IR、Python IR/DSL、导出和类型推导一致；非法 arity/type/layout 有负向 UT；只有存在清晰高层语义时才增加 tensor API。
- [ ] **G2 exact codegen**：codegen UT 断言精确 `pto.*` 名、operand/outs 顺序、属性与 enum；输出能够通过 pinned PTOAS assembler。类似名称或由其他 op 间接实现不算通过。
- [ ] **G3 真机 ST**：至少在一个支持平台执行真机同名 ST；按“ST 覆盖要求”完成该 op 在该平台适用的全部语义分支和 `valid_shape` case，比较可信 reference。其他声称支持但尚未真机验证的平台必须显式保留为待办；任何必需 case 缺失或依赖 skip/xpass 均不算该平台通过。
- [ ] **G4 专项集成**：MX/quant 使用 A5 scaling 约束；async prefetch 使用 context/session；comm 使用确定性双 rank hit/miss、session/event 一致性和 flat-contiguous-1D 限制。
- [ ] **G5 收口**：相关 UT/ST 全绿；至少一个支持平台具备真机同名执行证据后，可在本批变更中把状态矩阵 `❌` 改为 `✅` 并附证据，尚未验证的平台继续写入备注和 G3 待办。若 G0/G2/G3 暴露上游缺陷且没有任何平台通过，保留 `❌`，记录版本、平台和最小复现，不以“已有 frontend”代替完成。

## 高风险接口备注

- `tpow/tpows`：浮点或 high-precision 路径需要 `tmp`；纯整数路径必须省略 `tmp`。
- `tquant`：F32 source；SYM→I8 不带 offset，ASYM→UI8 需要 offset；A2/A3 可用 tmp 合成，A5 不带 tmp。`tquant.mx` 单独按 A5 验证。
- `tget_scale_addr` 与 MX 矩阵族：A5-only；scaling tile 的 loc、shape、valid shape、layout 必须满足 PTOAS 约束。
- `tmov.fp`：legacy 兼容项；新代码优先使用 `tmov` 的 FP operand 形式。
- async comm：session/event 必须成对匹配，put/get 当前只承诺 flat contiguous logical-1D。
- exact collectives：现有高层 collective 若最终只生成 `tput/tget`，不能作为 `tbroadcast/tgather/tscatter/treduce` 的完成证据。

## Background During the Qwen3-14B paged-attention migration to `aiv_shard`, assembling separate QK page tiles into columns of a wider Vec tile fails in the pinned A2/A3 toolchain. A 16-line standalone reproducer removes the model, shard/gather operations, runtime execution, and golden harness. PyPTO emits `pto.subview` plus `pto.tmov`, and PTOAS rejects that generated program. | Component | Reproduced version | |---|---| | pypto-lib | `0e7e07aa5e42db6e08c68fd5bfe1def571492b53` (`main`, with local Qwen experiments; full reproducer below) | | PyPTO | `9f657f37ed20ce148b46fb7229c267a152a0644e` (`main-test`, editable installation) | | simpler runtime | `4e4d3a4ad1e54c1db3d50e72decc025a9075bfa0` (detached, matches PyPTO gitlink) | | PTOAS | `0.57` (matches `toolchain/versions.env`) | | PTO ISA | `a8040450238f162985d8b596fbebeb54bfba2bf5` (detached, managed checkout matches runtime's `pto_isa.pin`) | | CANN | `9.0.0` | | Python / torch | `3.10.19` / `2.6.0+cpu` | | Host / target | Linux aarch64 / `a2a3` | The runtime source checkout and toolchain pins are consistent. The installed runtime binary's build revision was not independently stamped/verified. ### Component Codegen ### Description `pl.assemble(target, source, [0, 128])`, with FP32 Vec target `[16,512]` and source `[16,128]`, fails during PTOAS compilation: ```text 'pto.tmov' op expects A2/A3 non-mat tmov to use matching src/dst shapes ``` The public PyPTO [Vec assembly example](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/blob/9f657f37ed20ce148b46fb7229c267a152a0644e/examples/intermediate/05_assemble.py) documents column insertion. Reporting this against PyPTO Codegen because this supported source-level operation currently generates a program rejected by the pinned assembler. Whether the final fix belongs in the lowering or the PTOAS subview/TMOV contract remains to be determined. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Use the pinned environment above; source the CANN environment and set `PTOAS_ROOT` to the PTOAS 0.57 release root containing `ptoas.sh`. 2. Save the complete source below as `repro_vec_assemble.py`. 3. Run `python repro_vec_assemble.py`. No device allocation is required; `codegen_only=True` still invokes PTOAS.
Complete reproducer: repro_vec_assemble.py (save locally) ```python import torch import pypto.language as pl from pypto.runtime import RunConfig @pl.jit def assemble_columns(x: pl.Tensor[[16, 128], pl.FP32], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16, 512], pl.FP32]]): with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP): source = pl.load(x, [0, 0], [16, 128], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec) target = pl.tile.full([16, 512], dtype=pl.FP32, value=0.0) result = pl.assemble(target, source, [0, 128]) pl.store(result, [0, 0], out) return out if __name__ == '__main__': assemble_columns.compile(torch.zeros(16, 128), torch.zeros(16, 512), config=RunConfig(platform='a2a3', codegen_only=True)) ```
### Expected Behavior Compilation succeeds for inserting the `[16,128]` tile into columns 128 through 255 of a zero `[16,512]` Vec tile. If this target-specific assembly form is unsupported, emit a source-level diagnostic explaining the restriction. ### Actual Behavior ```text Failed to compile function 'assemble_columns_incore_0': ptoas compilation failed: error: 'pto.tmov' op expects A2/A3 non-mat tmov to use matching src/dst shapes ``` Generated PTO excerpt, with source-location annotations removed: ```mlir %target__ssa_v0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c8192_i64 valid_row = %c16_index valid_col = %c512_index : !pto.tile_buf pto.texpands ins(%cst_7 : f32) outs(%target__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf) %assemble_view = pto.subview %target__ssa_v0[%c0_index, %c128_index] sizes [16, 128] valid [%c16_index, %c128_index] : !pto.tile_buf -> !pto.tile_buf pto.tmov ins(%source__ssa_v0 : !pto.tile_buf) outs(%assemble_view : !pto.tile_buf) ``` Both printed TMOV operand types have logical dimensions `[16,128]`, while the destination view originates from a `[16,512]` allocation. A physical layout/pitch restriction is a hypothesis, not an independently established root cause. ### Git Commit ID `9f657f37ed20ce148b46fb7229c267a152a0644e` ### NPU Kind Other: `a2a3` compiler target. This reproducer only compiles; it does not execute on a device. ### Host Platform Linux (aarch64) ### Additional Context The lowering entry point is `MakeTileAssembleCodegenPTO` in `src/backend/common/pto_ops_datamove.cpp`. In the Qwen candidate, concatenating page results with `pl.concat` avoids this assembly failure and the tested output/cache comparisons pass. That workaround does not establish correctness of arbitrary column insertion or resolve this compiler/toolchain issue.
title: [Bug] Vec column assemble lowers to subview TMOV rejected by pinned PTOAS on A2/A3

## Background In pypto-lib, a scalar `pl.max` / `pl.min` on two FP32 scalars has a **compile** problem: codegen emits a `ptoas_bitcast(float)` helper **without the `__aicore__` qualifier**, so the AIV kernel cannot call it and the incore g++ compile fails. Reproduce with: python fp32_scalar_max.py 0 # needs a real a2a3 device The repro case is **not committed** — save the file below to run it. It imports `golden`, the validation harness that ships with `hw-native-sys/pypto-lib`, so run it from a pypto-lib checkout root.
Reproduction case — fp32_scalar_max.py ```python """Minimal repro: scalar pl.max on FP32 emits a ptoas_bitcast(float).""" import pypto.language as pl ROWS = 8 COLS = 64 @pl.jit def fp32_scalar_max( x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[1, 8], pl.FP32]], ): for _blk in pl.spmd(1, name_hint="fp32_scalar_max"): lane_maxima = pl.row_max(x) # [ROWS, 1] best = pl.read(lane_maxima, [0, 0]) # FP32 scalar for lane in pl.range(1, ROWS): best = pl.max(best, pl.read(lane_maxima, [lane, 0])) pl.write(out, [0, 0], best) return out if __name__ == "__main__": import sys import torch from golden import TensorSpec, run from pypto.runtime import RunConfig device = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 0 run( fn=fp32_scalar_max, specs=[ TensorSpec("x", [ROWS, COLS], torch.float32, init_value=torch.randn), TensorSpec("out", [1, 8], torch.float32), ], golden_fn=lambda t: None, config=RunConfig(platform="a2a3", device_id=device), ) ```
Reproduction environment: | Component | Version | |---|---| | pypto-lib | `e058d747` (branch: `main`) | | pypto | `9f657f37` (branch: `main`) | | simpler | `4e4d3a4a` (branch: detached) | | ptoas | `0.57` | | pto-isa | `a8040450` (branch: detached) | | CANN | `9.0.0` | All four components are exactly on their pins (pypto's `runtime` gitlink, `runtime/pto_isa.pin`, and `toolchain/versions.env`). Diagnosis: **pypto (Codegen)** — the emitted helper is missing `__aicore__`. ### Description `pl.max(a, b)` on two FP32 scalars lowers to a NaN- and signed-zero-aware select that inspects the sign bit via `ptoas_bitcast(v)`. Codegen emits that helper into the generated AIV source as a plain `static inline` template, while every other helper it emits into the same file carries `__aicore__`. AscendC therefore rejects the call from the `__aicore__` kernel body. From the generated `kernels/aiv/fp32_scalar_max_fp32_scalar_max.cpp` — note the qualifier on the sibling helper immediately above: ```cpp template static __aicore__ inline void PTOAS__DCCI_SINGLE_CACHE_LINE(Ptr ptr) { // <-- has __aicore__ dcci((__gm__ void*)ptr, cache_line_t::SINGLE_CACHE_LINE); } template static inline To ptoas_bitcast(From from) { // <-- missing __aicore__ static_assert(sizeof(To) == sizeof(From), "ptoas_bitcast: size mismatch"); To to; __builtin_memcpy(&to, &from, sizeof(To)); return to; } ``` and the call site inside the kernel: ```cpp static __aicore__ void fp32_scalar_max_fp32_scalar_max(__gm__ float* v1, ...) { ... float v28 = v26; float v29 = v23.GetValue(i27); uint32_t v30 = ptoas_bitcast(v28); // line 124 ``` The same expression on **INT32** scalars compiles and runs, so only the FP32 path reaches this helper. Two further notes: - **`--compile-only` does not catch this.** The failure is in the incore AIV compile, which only runs on a real device dispatch, so the whole class of generated-source defects is invisible to compile-only CI. - Reducing a handful of lane maxima to one scalar is the natural spelling for a two-stage vector reduction. Without it the kernel has to broadcast the partial reduction back across a tile and take a second column reduction purely to avoid the scalar op. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Save the reproduction case above into a `hw-native-sys/pypto-lib` checkout. 2. Run `python fp32_scalar_max.py 0` on a host with an a2a3 device. 3. Observe the AIV kernel compile fail before the dispatch. ### Expected Behavior The generated `ptoas_bitcast` helper is qualified `__aicore__` (like the other helpers emitted into the same translation unit), the AIV kernel builds, and the scalar FP32 `pl.max` / `pl.min` runs. ### Actual Behavior ``` kernels/aiv/fp32_scalar_max_fp32_scalar_max.cpp:124:20: error: no matching function for call to 'ptoas_bitcast' uint32_t v30 = ptoas_bitcast(v28); ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ kernels/aiv/fp32_scalar_max_fp32_scalar_max.cpp:62:20: note: candidate function not viable: call to [host] function from [aicore] function static inline To ptoas_bitcast(From from) { ^ 96 warnings and 1 error generated. ``` ### Git Commit ID 9f657f37 ### NPU Kind Ascend 910C ### Host Platform Linux (aarch64) ### Additional Context Present since at least 2026-08-18 and re-verified on 2026-09-06 against pypto `9f657f37` with pto-isa `a8040450` — still reproduces. Workaround in our model code: collapse the lane maxima with a vector reduction instead of a scalar loop, which costs an extra broadcast plus a second column reduction.
title: [Bug] Codegen emits ptoas_bitcast without __aicore__, so scalar FP32 pl.max/pl.min fails the AIV compile

## Background

In pypto-lib, `models/deepseek_v4_flash_mtp/prefill_fwd.py` (`l3_prefill_fwd`, the packed-prefill program DeepSeek-V4-Flash serving uses) on `a2a3` (8 devices) produces **NaN logits for any packed prefill extent above 128 tokens with real W8A8 weights** (extents 64/128 generate correctly; 129/160/256/302 fail deterministically). Full symptom details, extent table, and the follow-on AICore fault chain are in pypto-lib#1072 — that issue also shows pypto-lib's own standalone harness hides the NaNs (`[RUN] PASS (validation skipped)`).

A pypto-commit bisect of that failure (green `42881d7b` → red `57e5c315`) now localizes it:

| # | pypto | simpler | ptoas | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `42881d7b` | `799640e6` | 0.57 | ✅ correct greedy generation |
| 2 | `8cf3f058` (= 7542c36d's parent) | `799640e6` | 0.57 | ✅ correct greedy generation |
| 3 | `8cf3f058` | `0659e29b` | 0.57 | ✅ correct — simpler bump exonerated |
| 4 | `8cf3f058` | `799640e6` | 0.60 | ✗ assemble error: `'pto.tcvt' op requires explicit tmp ...` |
| 5 | **`7542c36d`** | `799640e6` | 0.57 | ✗ parse error: `expected ':'` (new .pto syntax) |
| 6 | **`7542c36d`** | `0659e29b` | 0.59 | ✗ assemble error: `'pto.tmrgsort' op format2 expects tmp.cols >= sum(src.cols) = 1024` |
| 7 | **`7542c36d`** | `0659e29b` | 0.60 | 🔴 **assembles; NaN logits for extents > 128** |

The seven commits between `42881d7b` and `7542c36d` are jointly exonerated (row 2 contains them all). The failure flips exactly at **`7542c36d` "Upgrade PTOAS to v0.60 and pin runtime to 0659e29 (#2523)"** — but that commit is an atomic bundle: its explicit-tmp `tcvt`/`tmrgsort` authoring changes (`python/pypto/ir/op/tile_ops.py`, `tensor_ops.py`, `language/op/*`) and PTOAS v0.60 **require each other** (rows 4–6), so old code only assembles on ≤0.57 and new code only on 0.60. The runtime (simpler) pin is not involved (row 3).

From a consumer (pypto-lib / pypto-serving) side the two halves of the bundle cannot be tested independently, so the regression is somewhere in the pair {new explicit-tmp lowering, PTOAS v0.60 assembly of it} — the pypto↔PTOAS split needs owner-side tooling (e.g. PTOAS 0.60 assembling a hand-written explicit-tmp repro, or pypto emitting the old-style form for a diff).

### Component

Codegen (explicit-tmp tcvt/tmrgsort lowering, introduced with the PTOAS v0.60 bump)

### Description

Since `7542c36d`, `l3_prefill_fwd`'s multi-tile walk corrupts outputs whenever a packed extent exceeds one 128-token tile — any second tile (including perfectly aligned ones: 256 = 2×128) produces NaN activations/logits. Requires real W8A8 weights (random-weight runs of the standalone harness don't show the serving-visible failure signature).

### Steps to Reproduce

Via pypto-serving (PR #204 head `a261960`; its KV-sizing ring-budget fix is required, otherwise a separate pooled-arena OOM masks this first):

```bash
pypto-serving \
  --model <w8a8 checkpoint dir> \
  --prompt "<' and' repeated 150 times> Huawei is" \
  --platform a2a3 --devices <8 free device ids> \
  --dp 8 --ep 8 --block-size 128 \
  --max-model-len 1024 --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --long-prefill-token-threshold 4096 \
  --generate-config '{"max_new_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0.0}' \
  --num-speculative-tokens 1 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --ring-dep-pool 131072 --ring-task-window 131072 --ring-heap 2147483648
```

Checkpoint: convert HF `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` with pypto-serving's `scripts/convert_deepseek_v4_to_w8a8.py`. Packed-extent sweep (prompt length): 64 ✅, 128 ✅, 129 ❌, 160 ❌, 256 ❌, 302 ❌ — deterministic across repeats.

The same flip is observable through pypto-lib 85e0790 alone: rows 2 vs 7 of the matrix above (its `models/deepseek_v4_flash_mtp/prefill_fwd.py` at `--num-tokens 160/302`), noting the stock golden harness skips validation and prints PASS unless outputs are dumped (see pypto-lib#1072).

### Expected Behavior

Correct greedy generation for any packed extent, as produced by `8cf3f058` + PTOAS v0.57 (rows 1–3).

### Actual Behavior

On `7542c36d`..main (`57e5c315`) + PTOAS v0.60:

```
WARNING | Sampler received non-finite logits
# ~3 s later, next program faults:
AICore 507015: "VEC instruction error: the ub address out of bounds (0x4000000000000000)"
# kernel: aicore_kernel_0_mix_aic (merged-binary KERNEL_ENTRY macro),
# task_id/func_id 15 -> kernel_config.py maps to qkv_proj_rope.py scopes
# (qr_proj_seed / qr_rms_norm_quant), launched with dynamic t_dim/T_TILE block count
```

The request then returns an empty completion; the lane is poisoned for subsequent requests.

### Git Commit ID

First bad: `7542c36dbfca87d36d2a1f5d3af1ac7a20a95f91` (reproduces through main tip `57e5c3153f3f8fbdfcc160e076a0becb3065e212`; parent `8cf3f05853a58b7745108acf45436029d302e948` is good)

### NPU Kind

Other: Ascend 910 — `a2a3` platform, 8 devices

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Bisect environment (all pins consistent per commit):

| Component | Version (good rows) | Version (bad rows) |
|---|---|---|
| pypto | `8cf3f058` or `42881d7b` | `7542c36d` |
| simpler | `799640e6` (also tested `0659e29b`) | `0659e29b` |
| pto-isa | `cd4a3d3f` (pin of `799640e6`) / `be5ccb76` (pin of `0659e29b`) | `be5ccb76` |
| ptoas | 0.57 | 0.60 |
| pypto-lib | `85e0790` | `85e0790` |
| pypto-serving | PR #204 head `a261960` | PR #204 head `a261960` |
| CANN | 9.0.0 | 9.0.0 |

Related: pypto-lib#1072 (full symptom analysis, device-log mapping, dumped-output NaN locations), pypto-serving#204 (CI `k1-prefix-cache` is the red test). Happy to run further discriminating experiments on this machine (device access available) — e.g. assembling a specific pypto-emitted `.pto` under different ptoas builds if that helps split the pair.

`docs/en/user/04-dev-container.md`, mirrored in `docs/zh/user/04-dev-container.md`:

The guide names `pypto-update.sh` as the **only** step that reinstalls ptoas when `toolchain/versions.env` moves the pin. It says the published image places the script, untracked, in the image's own checkout at `/workspace/pypto/.github/docker/`. It is not in this repository:

> | Codegen fails with `ptoas at '...' is version X, but PyPTO requires PTOAS >= vY` | The assembler has fallen behind `toolchain/versions.env` after a hand-run source update | `/workspace/pypto/.github/docker/pypto-update.sh` — it is the only step that reinstalls ptoas. The image as published is aligned (0.61) |

> **Only two of the three cases can run it.** The script lives in the image's own source tree, not in the repository and not on `PATH`, so a bind mount over `/workspace` hides it along with everything else the image had there.

A bind-mounted checkout is the usual way a user's source gets ahead of the image's ptoas. Following the table row there gives `No such file or directory`. The by-hand fallback (lines 385–393) only *checks* the version:

grep '^PTOAS_VERSION=' /workspace/pypto/toolchain/versions.env

The guide still documents its flags (`--no-pull`, `--reinstall-deps`, `--proxy`, `--remote-submodules`, `--jobs`, `--skip-doctor`) and its `git reset --hard origin/main` behaviour, none of which the repository can check.

- Not verified: that the published image (`sha256:ffa6bef8…`) actually contains the script, or the `/opt/pypto/ptoas` layout. The image was not pulled for this report.

### Summary

PyPTO cannot express PTOAS's *global-entry* pipe form. As a result a V2C (AIV->AIC) payload can only ever be a whole freshly-popped value; it cannot be delivered into a sub-region of an L1 tile the kernel already owns. This forces "one gather per whole matmul operand", which in turn inflates the cross-core slot size and makes otherwise-valid kernels unschedulable.

#### Current behaviour

`tile.tpop_from_aic` / `tile.tpop_from_aiv` are registered `.no_argument()` with `f_deduce_type(DeduceUnknownType)` (`src/ir/op/tile_ops/cross_core.cpp:248-270`), so the result is always a Tile pinned to the ring slot. The DSL intrinsic mirrors this — `pl.tpop_from_aiv(*, shape, dtype, split, id) -> Tile` is keyword-only with no destination parameter (`python/pypto/language/op/system_ops.py:294-333`), while `pl.tpush_to_aic(tile, ...)` does take its operand.

Consequently a DSL write of the form `dst_l1_tile[a:b, :] = pl.aic_gather(ub_tile)` lowers to tpop + `pto.subview` + `pto.tmov` with `loc=mat` on BOTH sides. A2A3 has no such tmov pair — PTOAS lists the supported A2A3 pairs as `mat -> left/right/bias/scaling`, `vec -> vec`, `acc -> mat`, `acc -> vec` (`ptoas/docs/PTO_IR_manual.md:1565-1571`). ptoas fails with:

```
'pto.tmov' op expects a supported tmov address-space pair for this target
  loc("build_output/.../ptoas/qk_pv.pto":70:9)
```

Generated IR at that point:

```mlir
%chunk = pto.tpop_from_aiv {split = 1} -> !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=bf16, rows=32, cols=512, ...>
%assemble_view = pto.subview %qk_kv[%micro_step, %c0] sizes [32, 512] valid [32, 512]
  : !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=bf16, rows=128, cols=512, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=512>
  -> !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=bf16, rows=32, cols=512, ...>
pto.tmov ins(%chunk : loc=mat ...) outs(%assemble_view : loc=mat ...)   // <-- no such instruction
```

### Motivation / Use Case

**Motivating kernel**

DeepSeek v4-flash sparse decode attention (pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_sparse_attn.py`, `qk_pv` SPMD region), reproduced with:

```
PTO_BENCH=1 python models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_attention_csa.py -d 1 --enable-l2-swimlane 1 --start-pos 8192
```

The kernel stages 128 scattered 1 KB KV rows into a `[128, 512]` BF16 L1 tile in `[32, 512]` micro-chunks, using two AIV lanes to gather (an AIV sustains far more outstanding scattered loads than the cube's ND2NZ path), then runs `Q @ KV^T` and `P @ KV` off the one resident L1 tile via `transpose_view`. Every on-chip budget fits (L1 128 KB of 512 KB, UB 16 KB per lane of 184 KB, Acc 80 KB of 128 KB); the design is blocked purely by the missing lowering. Working around it by gathering the whole `[128, 512]` tile in one shot makes the cross-core slot 128 KB and overruns the UB budget.

### Proposed API / Behavior

#### What PTOAS already supports

`pto.tpop_from_aiv` has a second result form (`ptoas/docs/PTO_IR_manual.md:9721-9755`):

```mlir
%entry = pto.tpop_from_aiv {id = 0, split = 1} -> !pto.tensor_view<...>
```

> for global entries this waits for producer ready and assigns the current GM FIFO slot address into the returned GlobalTensor-like descriptor [...] A global-entry pop does **not** perform `TLOAD`; callers explicitly load from the returned GM entry or from views derived from it

And (`ptoas/docs/PTO_IR_manual.md:9236-9241`):

> When every transfer op bound to one pipe id uses a global entry, the pipe is a **global-only GM FIFO**. Its frontend initialize op carries `gm_slot_tensor` and may carry `slot_num`; `gm_slot_buffer`, `c2v_consumer_buf`, `v2c_consumer_buf`, `local_slot_num`, `pto.reserve_buffer`, and `pto.import_reserved_buffer` are **not used**.

i.e. a global-only pipe reserves NO on-chip memory at all.

The destination-side machinery also already exists: `tile.gather_row` is documented as "Load one GM row directly into a sub-region of an on-chip tile (DPS) ... `pto.subview` of `dst` + `pto.tload`, GM -> on-chip, **no `pto.tmov`**" (`python/pypto/language/op/tile_ops.py:485-495`; codegen `src/backend/common/pto_ops_datamove.cpp:297`). It is DPS, takes a dynamic `dst_offset`, and accepts a Mat/L1 destination. It only needs a GM `Tensor` source — which is exactly what a global-entry pop returns.

The subview itself is already legal and already emitted: per the `pto.subview` verifier (`ptoas/docs/PTO_IR_manual.md:960-1020`), for boxed row-major tiles the subview must keep the full source column extent with column offset 0, and sizes must be multiples of the inner boxed shape; `[micro_step, 0] sizes [32, 512]` on a `[128, 512]` BF16 NZ tile (16x16 inner box) satisfies all of it, and "lowering keeps parent physical stride/base semantics".

#### Proposed change (all at the PyPTO level; no ISA or PTOAS work needed)

1. IR: add global-entry variants of `tile.tpop_from_aiv` / `tile.tpop_from_aic` whose result is a GM Tensor descriptor rather than a Tile, plus a producer-side `tile.talloc_to_aic` / `talloc_to_aiv`.
2. Lowering: when an `aic_gather` result feeds a `tile.assemble` into a Mat tile (the exact pattern that produces mat->mat tmov today), emit pop-entry -> subview -> tload -> tfree instead. The compiler already computes the subview and the offset at that point.
3. Pipe setup: mark that pipe id global-only — carry `gm_slot_tensor` + `slot_num`, drop `reserve_buffer` / `import_peer_buffer` / the consumer-buf args.
4. Verifier: no change expected. `AivSplitValid` rejects `tile.assemble` inside a `pl.split_aiv` region; under this lowering the assemble is gone and the cube-side tload/subview sit outside the region regardless.

Target DSL shape:

```python
entry = pl.tpop_entry_from_aiv(shape=[ATTN_K_TILE_MICRO, HEAD_DIM], dtype=pl.BF16, split=1)  # -> Tensor (GM slot)
qk_kv = pl.tile.gather_row(qk_kv, entry, [micro_step, 0], [0, 0], [ATTN_K_TILE_MICRO, HEAD_DIM])
pl.tfree_from_aiv(...)
```

#### Acceptance criteria

1. A V2C payload can be delivered into a sub-region of a caller-owned L1 tile with no `pto.tmov`.
2. A global-only pipe emits no `pto.reserve_buffer` and consumes no on-chip memory for the ring.
3. The motivating kernel above compiles and runs with `[32, 512]` micro-chunks.
4. Diagnostics: until/unless the lowering handles it, `InitMemRef` should reject "assemble a cross-core tpop result into another L1 tile" with a source-located error instead of letting it reach ptoas as an instruction-selection failure at a `.pto` line number. `init_memref.cpp:87,558,931` already tracks that a tpop result owns no general-pool buffer, so the information is available.

### Alternatives Considered

**Do NOT implement this as an `out=` parameter on the existing pop.**

The tile-entry pop re-bases its destination. From `pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a2a3/TPush.hpp:464-468`:

```cpp
uint64_t localTileBase = fifo.V2C_CONSUMER_BUF +
    (tileIndex % RingFiFo::LOCAL_SLOT_NUM) * ConsM * ConsN * sizeof(T);
TASSIGN_IMPL(tile, localTileBase);   // overwrites the destination base address
TLOAD_IMPL(tile, globalTensor);
```

A DPS destination on that form would be silently discarded. The destination-honouring path must be the global-entry form, which performs no TLOAD.

**Gather the whole tile in one shot.** Working around the missing lowering by gathering the entire `[128, 512]` operand in a single transfer makes the cross-core slot 128 KB, which overruns the UB budget — so this is not a viable workaround for the motivating kernel.

### Additional Context

| Field | Value |
| ----- | ----- |
| Git Commit ID | `7d743e8d35bfd45df2b09a08b6a79308fada1342` |
| NPU Kind | Ascend 910B (backend target `Ascend910B` / A2A3) |
| Host Platform | Linux (aarch64) |

Related: #1820 (explicit AIV split RFC — `aiv_shard` / `aic_gather` surface this lowering gap), #2040 (A2/A3 C2V/V2C GM round-trip cost), #2269 (GM pipe workspace sizing), #2077 (keeping matmul operands resident in L1).
title: [Feature] Support PTOAS global-entry V2C pipe so a cross-core payload can land in a sub-region of an L1 tile

## Summary

PTOAS 0.65 resolves [PTOAS#1570](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1570), but PyPTO still rejects a scale-bearing `Acc/L0C -> Mat/L1` FIXPIPE writeback on A2/A3 through `FixpipeEpilogueValid`.

This blocks the Cube score-reduction implementation in [pypto-lib#1354](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-lib/pull/1354), even though its CI installs PTOAS 0.65.

Related feature request: #2765.

## Reproduction

```python
score_i32 = pl.tile.matmul(query_i8, kv_i8_t)
score_relu = pl.tile.create(
    [64, 512],
    pl.FP16,
    target_memory=pl.Mem.Mat,
)
score_relu = pl.tile.assemble(
    score_relu,
    score_i32,
    [0, 0],
    pre_quant=1.0 / 1024,
    pre_relu=True,
)
```

Compile for `a2a3` with PTOAS 0.65.

## Actual behavior

Compilation fails immediately after `InferTileMemorySpace`:

```text
ERROR - FixpipeEpilogueValid

tile.assemble carries a pre_quant scale on the Acc -> Mat writeback,
which the 'a2a3' backend withholds: ptoas assembles the scale but emits
a pto-isa call that silently drops it (PTOAS#1570).
```

Observed in the pypto-lib `sim (a2a3sim)` job with:

- PyPTO: `8a944cf211a847b9d39d35a38791fd5d5bd2120d`
- PTOAS: `v0.65`
- failing pypto-lib job: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-lib/actions/runs/35727007507/job/106743083641

Both `models/deepseek_v4_flash_dspark/decode_csa.py` and `decode_indexer.py` fail at compile time. The simulator never runs.

## Expected behavior

On toolchains containing the PTOAS#1570 fix, PyPTO should allow the supported A2/A3 form:

- source: INT32 accumulator in L0C
- destination: FP16 Mat tile in L1
- `pre_quant`: scalar FP32 scale (`DEQF16`)
- optional `pre_relu=True`

The generated `pto.tinsert`/FIXPIPE call must retain the scale and use the correct scaled overload.

## Suggested scope

1. Enable the appropriate `SupportsFixpipePreQuant(..., FixpipeDest::kMat, ...)` capability for A2/A3 when using the supported PTOAS toolchain.
2. Update `FixpipeEpilogueValid` behavior and its diagnostics/docs, which currently state that Acc-to-Mat `pre_quant` is withheld on every backend because of PTOAS#1570.
3. Add a codegen test for `INT32 Acc -> FP16 Mat` with both `pre_quant` and `pre_relu`.
4. Add a compile or simulator test that feeds the resulting L1 FP16 tile into a second Cube matmul.
5. Keep unsupported dtype, destination, and backend combinations rejected with a clear diagnostic.

## Why this matters

The DSpark CSA indexer currently moves a large per-head score intermediate to Vector for broadcast, multiply, and reduction. The new path performs:

```text
INT8 QK MatMul
  -> INT32 L0C
  -> FIXPIPE scale + ReLU into FP16 L1
  -> FP16 coefficient MatMul on Cube
  -> reduced Score to Vector for TopK
```

At TP1/B16/128K, the downstream implementation reduces standalone Indexer latency from 1246.3 us to 1015.6 us and full CSA latency from 1882.9 us to 1642.2 us. It cannot pass upstream CI until PyPTO recognizes the PTOAS 0.65 capability.
title: [Bug] Enable scaled L0C-to-L1 FIXPIPE writeback with PTOAS 0.65

### Component

Codegen

### Description

PyPTO emits a degenerate tile whose valid extents are the **constant zero** (`valid_row = %c0_index valid_col = %c0_index`). On the `memory_planner=MemoryPlanner.PTOAS` path that zero is additionally baked into the static view annotation of the consuming op (`v_row=0, v_col=0`), so ptoas instantiates `pto::Tile<..., 0, 0, ...>` in the generated C++ — and pto-isa models only two states:

```cpp
// build/pto-isa/include/pto/common/pto_tile.hpp
AICORE static constexpr std::enable_if_t<(RowMask > 0), unsigned> GetValidRow()
AICORE std::enable_if_t<RowMask == DYNAMIC, unsigned> GetValidRow() const
```

`RowMask = 0` satisfies neither, so the incore C++ compile fails with no matching overload.

The degenerate tile itself is emitted under **both** planners — this is not PTOAS-specific. The PyPTO path annotates the consuming op dynamically (`v_row=?, v_col=?`), which becomes `Tile<..., -1, -1, ...>`, compiles, and is a no-op at runtime. So the defect is latent on the default path and only becomes a hard error once the static annotation is used.

### Steps to Reproduce

The `.pto` and the generated C++ are produced without an NPU; only the final incore C++ compile needs the pto-isa headers.

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$(pwd)/python:$PYTHONPATH

python -m pytest "tests/st/runtime/cross_core/test_split_reduce_parity.py::test_none_split_row_sum_is_correct" \
  --platform=a2a3 --memory-planner=ptoas --precompile-workers=2 \
  --save-kernels --kernels-dir /tmp/ptoas

grep -n "v_row=0, v_col=0" /tmp/ptoas/split_reduce_parity_none_direct@a2a3@ptoas/ptoas/*.pto
grep -n "RowMajor, 0, 0" /tmp/ptoas/split_reduce_parity_none_direct@a2a3@ptoas/kernels/aiv/*.cpp
```

Affected cases:

- `tests/st/runtime/cross_core/test_split_reduce_parity.py::test_none_split_row_sum_is_correct[split_reduce_parity_none_direct]`
- `tests/st/runtime/cross_core/test_split_reduce_parity.py::test_none_split_row_sum_is_correct[split_reduce_parity_none_reshape]`

### Expected Behavior

PyPTO does not hand a statically-zero valid extent to the static view annotation. Either the degenerate tile is eliminated upstream, or its consuming op keeps the dynamic annotation, which is what the PyPTO path already does and what compiles.

### Actual Behavior

```text
build/pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a2a3/TDivS.hpp:305:29: error: no matching member function for call to 'GetValidRow'
        (dstValidRow == src.GetValidRow() && dstValidCol == src.GetValidCol())) {
                        ~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~
note: in instantiation of function template specialization
  'pto::TRECIP<pto::RecipAlgorithm::DEFAULT,
     pto::Tile<pto::TileType::Vec, float, 1, 16, pto::BLayout::RowMajor, -1, -1, ...>,
     pto::Tile<pto::TileType::Vec, float, 1, 16, pto::BLayout::RowMajor,  0,  0, ...>>'
note: candidate template ignored: requirement '0 > 0' was not satisfied [with RowMask = 0]
note: candidate template ignored: requirement '0 == DYNAMIC' was not satisfied [with RowMask = 0]
```

The emitted `.pto` under PTOAS bakes the zero into the consuming op's annotation:

```text
%8 = pto.alloc_tile valid_row = %c0_index valid_col = %c0_index : !pto.tile_buf<..., v_row=?, v_col=?, ...>
pto.trecip ins(%20 : !pto.tile_buf<..., v_row=0, v_col=0, ...>) outs(%8 : ...)
```

Under PyPTO the same `alloc_tile` carries `valid_row = %c0_index` too, but the consuming op stays dynamic and therefore compiles:

```text
%8 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c73728_i64 valid_row = %c0_index valid_col = %c0_index : !pto.tile_buf<..., v_row=?, v_col=?, ...>
pto.trecip ins(%8 : !pto.tile_buf<..., v_row=?, v_col=?, ...>) outs(%9 : ...)
```

### Git Commit ID

33476eadb4bd5cb3b505b748d402a6346d1b1a35

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Confirmed that the PyPTO-side fix is sufficient: replacing `v_row=0, v_col=0` with `v_row=?, v_col=?` in the emitted `.pto` and re-running ptoas 0.64 at `--pto-level=level2` makes the `Tile<..., 0, 0, ...>` instantiation disappear — only `-1, -1` and `1, 16` remain, and the result compiles.

Worth noting for the ptoas side as well: ptoas accepted `v_row=0` without complaint and emitted C++ that pto-isa cannot compile. A guard there would turn a confusing template-instantiation error into a clear diagnostic.

Related: #2557 — the same static-view / valid-extent annotation machinery, gated on a different axis.

Found while validating a suite-wide switch of the system tests to the ptoas planner: #2847.
title: [Bug] Zero valid_shape baked into the PTOAS view annotation emits uncompilable RowMask=0 tiles

### Summary

`pypto.jit._toolchain._console_interpreter()` rejects the console script that current pip generates for the `ptoas` entry point. On hosts where ptoas is installed from the release wheel with a recent pip, `capture_toolchain` reports an unusable identity, so the persistent JIT cache silently bypasses on every request and never turns on.

### Environment

- pypto @ `04f1f510` (main), installed with `pip install -e ".[dev]"`
- ptoas 0.61 from the GitHub release wheel (`ptoas-0.61-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_34_aarch64.whl`), installed with pip 26.1.2 into a conda env

### Observed

`$PREFIX/bin/ptoas` as generated by pip 26:

```python
#!/.../bin/python3.12
import sys
from ptoas._cli import main
if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.argv[0] = sys.argv[0].removesuffix('.exe')
    sys.exit(main())
```

`_CONSOLE_BODIES` (`pypto/jit/_toolchain.py:296`) only accepts the two older templates (the `re.sub(r'(-script\.pyw|\.exe)?$', ...)` form and the `-script.pyw`/`.exe` slicing form), so the AST-equality check in `_console_interpreter` raises `Unsupported PTOAS console-script grammar` and every component of `capture_toolchain` fails with it:

```
pypto: Unsupported PTOAS console-script grammar: .../bin/ptoas;
runtime: Unsupported PTOAS console-script grammar: ...;
pto_isa: Unsupported PTOAS console-script grammar: ...;
ptoas: Unsupported PTOAS console-script grammar: ...;
device_toolchain: Unsupported PTOAS console-script grammar: ...
```

With `PYPTO_CACHE=1`, `pypto.cache_stats().bypasses` increments on every JIT call and `last_bypass_reason` shows the grammar rejection, so the persistent cache never engages. Rewriting the launcher to the `re.sub` template (functionally identical) makes `capture_toolchain` pass, which confirms the template whitelist is the only blocker.

### Impact

Any deployment installing ptoas from the release wheel with a current pip silently loses persistent JIT caching — compilation still works, the cache just never enables. It also blocks the pypto-serving integration that routes `--use-compile-cache` through this cache: its READY-reuse acceptance asserts zero bypasses and fails on such hosts.

### Suggestion

Add the `sys.argv[0].removesuffix('.exe')` template to `_CONSOLE_BODIES`, or match the entry-point shim semantically instead of by exact AST equality — the three known templates are behaviorally identical.
title: [jit] Persistent cache always bypasses with wheel-installed ptoas: pip 26 console-script grammar rejected

### Component

Parser

### Description

An annotated scalar assignment whose right-hand side is an `INDEX`-typed **non-constant**
expression produces IR that violates `AssignTypeSymmetry`: the `Var` is stamped with the
annotation's dtype while the RHS keeps `INDEX`.

```python
v: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32] = pl.cast(i, pl.INT32) + 1
```

parses to `AssignStmt(Var[INT32], Add[INDEX])`. The malformed IR survives the whole pass
pipeline and fails inside PTOAS with an MLIR SSA-numbering error that names neither the
variable nor the user's line.

Root cause is in `python/pypto/language/parser/ast_parser.py`. The scalar branch at
`1845-1850` adopts the annotation as `override_type` for **any** `INDEX`-typed RHS:

```python
elif (
    isinstance(resolved, ir.ScalarType)
    and isinstance(value_expr.type, ir.ScalarType)
    and value_expr.type.dtype == DataType.INDEX
):
    override_type = resolved
```

but the re-typing that follows at `1862` only handles `ir.ConstInt`:

```python
if isinstance(override_type, ir.ScalarType) and isinstance(value_expr, ir.ConstInt):
    value_expr = ir.ConstInt(value_expr.value, override_type.dtype, value_expr.span)
```

So `acc: pl.Scalar[pl.INT64] = 0` is handled, and a non-constant `INDEX` RHS is not. The
comment directly above `1862` states this asymmetry is exactly what that re-stamp exists to
prevent.

What makes this more than cosmetic is that the annotation **defeats a type check that
otherwise works**. Unannotated, the same expression is correctly rejected at its use site:

```
Error: pl operation 'write': tensor.write requires value dtype to match tensor dtype,
       but got value dtype index and tensor dtype int32
```

Adding `: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32]` launders the mismatch into the Var's label and it passes.

Nothing catches it downstream. `AssignTypeSymmetry` is registered in
`src/ir/verifier/property_verifier_registry.cpp:114`, but no pass on this path declares the
property, so it never runs — confirmed still silent at `VerificationLevel.ROUNDTRIP`. That
detection half is already tracked as #1285 (the verifier landed; wiring it as a structural
property that `VerificationInstrument` checks did not). This issue is about the **producer**.

Not a print -> parse artefact: the round trip is byte-stable, preserving the asymmetry
faithfully rather than creating it, and unannotated source prints back as
`pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX]`, which is symmetric.

### Steps to Reproduce

Frontend only — no device, no distributed config:

```python
import pypto.language as pl

@pl.program
class P:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
    def k(self, out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[1, 1], pl.INT32]]) -> pl.Tensor[[1, 1], pl.INT32]:
        for i in pl.range(4):
            v: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32] = pl.cast(i, pl.INT32) + 1
            pl.write(out, [0, 0], v)
        return out

print(P)
```

prints the asymmetric binding:

```python
v: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32] = pl.cast(pl.cast(i, pl.INT32), pl.INDEX) + 1
```

Compiling any kernel that feeds such a value to an operand codegen casts via
`EmitCastToI32` fails. Minimal end-to-end case, using `pld.system.wait(expected=...)`:

```
barrier_rounds.pto:43:54: error: use of value '%2' expects different type than prior uses:
                          'i32' vs 'index'
```

`src/codegen/pto/pto_scalar_expr_codegen.cpp:314` dispatches on the IR-level type, reads the
Var's `INT32`, concludes no cast is needed, and emits the `index` SSA into an `i32` operand.

### Expected Behavior

`v: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32] = <INDEX expression>` should bind a `Var[INT32]` to an `INT32`-typed
value — the annotation re-types the RHS the same way it already does for an int literal — so
the assignment is symmetric and codegen emits `i32` arithmetic.

Failing that, the parser should reject the annotation with a diagnostic at the user's line
rather than emitting IR that dies inside PTOAS.

### Actual Behavior

`AssignStmt(Var[INT32], <INDEX expr>)` is emitted, survives all 54 passes unchecked, and
fails in PTOAS with an SSA-level type error that points at neither the variable nor the
source line.

### Git Commit ID

e806abbf (upstream/main 7ce27b0e)

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Working spellings today, for anyone hitting this:

- `pl.cast(e + 1, pl.INT32)` — cast once, at the end
- `epoch = pl.cast(e, pl.INT32) + 1` unannotated, where an `INDEX` value is acceptable

Found while reproducing #2778; it is not a prerequisite for that issue, whose own
reproduction is unannotated and compiles.

Suggested fix: extend the `1862` re-stamp beyond `ir.ConstInt` so a non-constant `INDEX` RHS
is wrapped in an explicit cast to the annotated dtype, keeping the existing
"annotation determines dtype" semantics consistent between constants and expressions. Scope
it to integral/`INDEX` pairs — `validate_annotation_consistency` already rejects an int
literal under a float annotation.
title: [Bug] Scalar annotation over an INDEX expression produces an asymmetric AssignStmt that fails in PTOAS

body:
## Background

In pypto-lib, the DeepSeek-V4 Flash MTP routed-expert kernel
(`models/deepseek_v4_flash_mtp/expert_routed.py`) wants its INT8 grouped-matmul
weight operands read **around L2**: the weight tile of each `(expert, row-tile)`
work item is streamed once and never revisited, so every L2 allocation it makes
is a guaranteed dead allocation that also evicts the activations which *do* get
reused. Measured on device by hand-editing the generated C++, the L2-bypass half
alone is worth **-7.9% on the routed-expert kernel / -2.8% of a whole decode
step**, and it is the larger of the two effects tracked in
hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#1039.

pypto already has the entire front end for this — `pl.set_cache_policy(t, pl.CachePolicy.BYPASS)`
and `pl.load(..., cache=...)`, shipped in #2540 — and the declaration reaches
codegen intact. `MakeTileLoadCodegenPTO` then **drops it**: it emits a warning
and an ordinary cached `pto.tload`. That was correct when it was written, and
the code says so:

```cpp
// src/backend/common/pto_ops_memory.cpp:113
// TEMPORARY (pypto #2534): PTOAS has no L2-bypass path yet
// (https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1356), so a BYPASS request is
// carried through the IR but compiles as an ordinary cached access. When that
// issue closes, this warn is REPLACED in place by
// `GetOrCreateTensorView(tensor, policy)` against an addptr-rooted view — the
// declaration already reaches here, so nothing upstream changes.
```

**PTOAS 0.61 now has that path.** This issue asks for the in-place replacement
the comment already anticipates — with one simplification: 0.61 takes an
attribute on `pto.tload`, so no addptr-rooted view is needed.

Reproduce with:

    python repro_cache_policy.py

Reproduction environment:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `b445fe7e` (branch: `perf/optimize-dspark-moe-balanced-routing`) |
| pypto | `8ffd67fe` (branch: `main`) |
| simpler | `4e4d3a4a` (detached) |
| ptoas | `0.61` |
| pto-isa | `a8040450` (detached) |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |

Version mismatch (off pinned): ptoas expected `0.60` (`toolchain/versions.env`),
actual `0.61`. The divergence is deliberate — 0.61 is the first release that
implements the PTOAS side, so the pin needs to move too (see Proposed API /
Behavior).

Diagnosis: **pypto** — the assembler feature exists and the DSL declaration
exists; only the codegen hop between them is missing.

### Summary

`CachePolicy.BYPASS` is accepted by the DSL, survives every pass, and is then
discarded in codegen: `pto.tload` is emitted without a `cache_policy` attribute
and a `[CacheBypassUnsupported]` warning is logged instead. Generated code is
byte-identical with and without the declaration, so the feature is currently a
no-op end to end.

PTOAS 0.61 implements `cache_policy` on `pto.tload`:

```python
>>> from ptoas.mlir.dialects import pto
>>> list(pto.LoadCachePolicy.__members__)
['Default', 'L2Bypass']
>>> pto.LoadCachePolicyAttr.get(pto.LoadCachePolicy.L2Bypass, ctx)
#pto.load_cache_policy<l2_bypass>
```

Taking pypto's **own generated** `.pto` for the repro below, adding that
attribute to the weight `pto.tload` by hand, and re-running ptoas 0.61
(`--enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level3`) changes exactly one line of the
emitted CCE:

```diff
-  TLOAD(v45, v50);
+  TLOAD<pto::TLoadL2Hint::NotAllocKeep>(v45, v50);
```

That is a native pto-isa L2 hint — cleaner than the architecture-specific
`ptr + 0x80000000000ULL` address alias the original request assumed, which is
what pypto-lib had to hand-edit into the generated C++ to measure the numbers
above.

### Motivation / Use Case

Any GEMM operand that is streamed once and never revisited: the weight tile of a
grouped/batched matmul, any operand whose working set exceeds L2, one-shot
activation reloads. In the DeepSeek-V4 Flash decode MoE this is the dominant
term — measured per-tile-count on one a2a3 card, 100 rounds after 20 warmup,
`effective_us` mean, every point carrying its own baseline repeat (drift
0.03-0.57%):

| tiles | % of decode layers | L2 bypass's own share |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | 12.0% | -3.8 pp |
| 16 | 15.7% | -5.3 pp |
| 18 | 8.5% | -6.2 pp |
| 20 | 3.0% | -9.7 pp |
| 27 | 1.8% | -11.3 pp |

The effect **grows** with case size, because what it protects is the activation
working set the streamed weights would otherwise evict.

### Proposed API / Behavior

No DSL change — the front end is already there. In `MakeTileLoadCodegenPTO`,
replace the warn with an attribute on the emitted `pto.tload`:

```
pto.tload ins(%w_pview : ...) outs(%wt : ...) {cache_policy = #pto.load_cache_policy<l2_bypass>}
```

`CachePolicy.DEFAULT` keeps emitting no attribute, so nothing changes for code
that does not declare a policy. The MX `layout` attribute and `cache_policy` can
co-occur, so the emit site needs to join a list rather than print one attribute.

Requires PTOAS >= 0.61 (older releases reject the attribute), so it also needs
`PTOAS_VERSION` in `toolchain/versions.env` moved from `v0.60` to `v0.61` — or
the emit gated on the configured assembler version.

Reproduction case — `repro_cache_policy.py` (not committed; save anywhere and run):

```python
"""CachePolicy.BYPASS is dropped in codegen: no cache_policy on pto.tload.

    python repro_cache_policy.py
"""
import pypto.language as pl
from pypto.runtime import RunConfig

M = N = K = 256


@pl.jit
def mm_bypass(
    a: pl.Tensor[[M, K], pl.FP32],
    b: pl.Tensor[[K, N], pl.FP32],
    c: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]],
):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="mm"):
        pl.set_cache_policy(b, pl.CachePolicy.BYPASS)
        ta = a[:, :]
        tb = b[:, :]
        c[:, :] = pl.matmul(ta, tb)
    return c


if __name__ == "__main__":
    compiled = mm_bypass.compile(config=RunConfig(platform="a2a3"))
    print("compiled:", compiled)
```

Observed output (compile succeeds; the declaration is dropped):

```text
[warning] [CacheBypassUnsupported] tensor 'b' requests CachePolicy.BYPASS, but PTOAS
has no L2-bypass path yet (https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1356);
compiling as an ordinary cached access at <repro-dir>/repro_cache_policy.py:20:9
```

Compiling the same kernel with and without the `pl.set_cache_policy` line and
diffing the two work dirs: `kernels/aic/mm.cpp` and `ptoas/mm.cpp` are byte-identical,
and `ptoas/mm.pto` differs only in `loc(...)` source line numbers.

### Additional Context

- Front end / docs: #2540, `docs/en/dev/language/05-cache-policy.md` (its
  "Current status" section is what this issue closes).
- PTOAS side: hw-native-sys/PTOAS#1356 — implemented in 0.61, though the issue
  is still open there.
- Related: hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#1039 (umbrella, carries the device measurements), #2534.
title: [Feature] Emit the declared GM cache policy as PTOAS's tload cache_policy attribute
